cli.failures.error_line.tone: terse, plain, states what the user typed wrong
cli.failures.error_line.note: Wraps every argparse usage failure, printed on stderr after the usage block. {prog} is the command path such as `lop teams show` and {message} is the already-localised failure sentence; both are inserted verbatim, so do not translate or reorder their content. Keep the shape '<command>: <error word>: <message>'.

cli.failures.required.tone: terse, plain, states what the user typed wrong
cli.failures.required.note: Missing required argument(s). {names} is a comma-separated list of argument names, flag spellings or dest names (technical tokens, inserted verbatim).

cli.failures.invalid_choice.tone: terse, plain, states what the user typed wrong
cli.failures.invalid_choice.note: A value that is not one of the allowed choices, for a flag or for the subcommand position (an unknown subcommand takes this same shape). {argument} is the flag or dest token, {value} is the user's input already quoted with its quote marks, {choices} is a comma-separated list of command or option tokens; all three stay verbatim.

cli.failures.invalid_command.tone: terse, plain, states what the user typed wrong
cli.failures.invalid_command.note: Raised when a command group is invoked without a valid verb. {group} is a command name such as config or agents and {command} is the verb typed or the literal word None when none was given; both stay verbatim, translate only 'Invalid' and 'command'.
